edges.limitations: The severe phenotype requires homozygosity: heterozygous p53+/Δ31 mice are only mildly affected, whereas every reported patient is heterozygous. The homozygous mice model dyskeratosis congenita, with short telomeres and pulmonary fibrosis, more closely than they model the Diamond-Blackfan-like erythroid failure of the human disease.

nodes.description: Heterozygous germline frameshift variants near the 3' end of TP53 remove the C-terminal domain while leaving the core DNA-binding domain intact. In the defining report both variants produced the same truncation, deleting 32 residues, and the mutant protein showed augmented transcriptional activity. This is the opposite direction of effect from the DNA-binding-domain variants of Li-Fraumeni syndrome. Recorded as GAIN_OF_FUNCTION following the sources' own wording ("activating", "gain-of-function"); the reported effect is increased transactivation by the truncated protein, not a novel activity.

nodes.description: The central node. Constitutively augmented p53 target-gene transactivation in every cell carrying the allele. The authors of the defining report frame the disease as confirming that p53 activation itself can cause an inherited bone marrow failure syndrome, rather than only accompanying the ribosomal, telomere or DNA-repair defects of other such syndromes. Here p53 activation is the primary lesion rather than a downstream consequence.
